title: A disabled Input still repaints its border on hover
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: Reverting the guard fails the new test: `npx vitest run src/components/Input.hover.test.tsx` exits 1 with `expected true to be false`, the disabled wrapper matching a rule that should not reach it, and exits 0 with the guard. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run, 628 tests, visual:compare 94/94 at 0 differing pixels, axe violations 0.

details:
`components/Input.md:108` says a disabled Input suppresses hover effects.

`src/styles/components/input.css:162` sets `border-color: var(--muted)` on the wrapper's `:hover` with no disabled guard. That class sits on the wrapper `<div>` at `src/components/Input.tsx:72`, and the native `disabled` attribute on the inner control does not affect a wrapper.

Hovering a disabled field therefore still moves the border colour, so the disabled affordance is weaker than the specification promises.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

Guarded by class rather than by `:disabled`, because the rule is on the wrapper div and the native attribute sits on the control inside it. The test asserts the rule's reach rather than the painted colour: a real `:hover` needs a real cursor, and neither the provider pointer nor a synthetic event moves the computed border in a headless browser, so a colour assertion would have passed with or without the fix. That was caught by writing the enabled case as a control first.
